findings.reason: atalk_route_packet() (net/appletalk/ddp.c:1287) receives a remote AppleTalk DDP packet forwarded by atalk_rcv() when no local interface matches (atalk_rcv calls pskb_may_pull(sizeof(*ddp)) then ddp = ddp_hdr(skb) at net/appletalk/ddp.c:1409, and passes that raw head pointer into atalk_route_packet(skb, dev, ddp, len_hops, origlen) at line 1447). len_hops comes straight from the attacker-controlled deh_len_hops field (ntohs(ddp->deh_len_hops), line 1411). Inside atalk_route_packet, skb_trim(skb, ...) (line 1333) is called with an attacker-influenced length; when the trimmed length is below the current skb->len, the trim resolves to ___pskb_trim() (net/core/skbuff.c:2515), which first does pskb_expand_head(skb, 0, 0, GFP_ATOMIC) whenever skb_cloned(skb) (net/core/skbuff.c:2524-2525) -- the classic reallocation that allocates a new data buffer and memcpy's the old head, freeing it. Immediately after the trim, the saved pre-trim pointer is written through at line 1338 (ddp->deh_len_hops = htons(len_hops)), i.e. a stale write into the old freed head (and stale writes also occur in the later else-branch skb_unshare path context). An attacker reaches this with a received DDP frame that has deh_dnet/deh_dnode matching a routed network but no local interface, on an skb that is cloned (e.g. delivered via a packet socket tap/clone on receive) and non-linear/oversized so the trim actually fires pskb_expand_head. Counterevidence checked: if skb_cloned() is false and skb->data_len is 0, __pskb_trim reduces to __skb_trim which only moves skb->tail and never reallocates, so the bug needs the cloned (or paged) receive path; the write happens unconditionally after the trim regardless of skb_trim's internal path, so the pointer is used without any re-derivation. This is a hypothesis from source reading, not a run-time KASAN confirmation.
findings.conclusion: atalk_route_packet writes through the ddp pointer captured before skb_trim(), which can call pskb_expand_head on a cloned skb and free the old head, yielding a stale-pointer write (UAF) on received DDP packets.

candidates.reason: skb_trim() at line 1333 can reach ___pskb_trim()->pskb_expand_head() when the skb is cloned (net/core/skbuff.c:2524) and thus reallocate the head; the ddp pointer derived from the old head (saved in atalk_rcv at line 1409 via ddp_hdr(skb)) is dereferenced for write at line 1338 after the trim with no re-fetch.
candidates.conclusion: Stale ddp head pointer is written after skb_trim() may have reallocated the cloned skb head in atalk_route_packet(); needs runtime confirmation of the cloned non-linear receive path.

coverage_gaps: Static review of the 480 helper call sites in net/ and drivers/net/ was only begun (a whole-function pointer-liveness scanner was written but produced no output before the session was cut), so the other ~479 pskb_expand_head/skb_cow/skb_linearize/pskb_trim/pskb_carve/skb_copy_expand_head sites in snapshots/s01 remain unreviewed.
limitations: No run-time reproduction was performed (no build or KASAN harness), so the pskb_expand_head reallocation on the cloned-receive path is inferred from the skb_cloned() branch in ___pskb_trim() (net/core/skbuff.c:2524-2525) rather than observed.

AppleTalk must be configured (an atalk interface and route) and the skb must arrive cloned and with len above the trim target for the reallocating trim to fire; if skbs are never cloned on that receive path the write stays in-bounds and the issue is latent.
The scanner used for candidate enumeration had a defect (it emitted no output for any of the 262 files), so coverage of this branch beyond the manually confirmed ddp.c case is not established.
